text:
sara_cust: Hey support — customer reports streaming connection drops consistently ~40–60s after start. They see a 403 mid-stream (not immediate). Request id from response header: rcx-9b2f-4411. Endpoint: /v1/streams/generate. Using cookie session + short-lived bearer refresh. Any quick repro steps we can ask them for?

maya_support: Thanks — can you grab a minimal curl that reproduces? Key things we need: full request headers, client-side timing (when token refresh happened), the exact request-id, and a verbose curl trace. Ask them to run with -v -N --no-buffer and keep the auth exact as their app. Also a timestamp in ms for when the 403 happened.

sara_cust: They tried this minimal reproduction but still flaky, sending it here: 

```
curl -v -N --no-buffer \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN" \
  -H "User-Agent: AcmeClient/1.2" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  --cookie "session=abcd1234; Path=/; HttpOnly" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-large&stream=true"
```

They say token is rotated by their app at ~50s after connect. 403 occurs at 51s. Request-id in the 403 response header matched rcx-9b2f-4411.

lucas_eng: Can we get them to include a couple extras so we can correlate server logs: 
- Add header X-Client-Ts-ms with current epoch ms at connect and again when they refresh the token.
- Confirm whether they re-connect or attempt to re-use the socket after refresh.
- Run curl with --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt to capture low-level stream frames.

Example curl to ask them to run (copy/paste, replace placeholders):

```
export TOKEN="<short_lived_token>" 
export SESS_COOKIE="session=abcd1234"
curl -v -N --no-buffer --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "User-Agent: AcmeClient/1.2" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "X-Client-Ts-ms: $(date +%s%3N)" \
  --cookie "${SESS_COOKIE}" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-large&stream=true"
```

Ask them to save /tmp/trace.txt and the full response headers and attach both. Also tell them to capture the exact epoch ms when they rotate the token and include that in the support ticket.

olga_oncall: If they can, add a short patch to send the new Authorization header over a fresh connection instead of trying to reuse the same TCP/TLS socket during rotation — that will help us determine if the proxy layer rejects mid-stream header swaps. If they must reuse socket, please include the client-side logs showing header set calls.

maya_support: Also ask them to include the response header set for the 403 (full headers) — sometimes proxies attach an X-Upstream-Err or x-request-id we can match to infra logs. We already have rcx-9b2f-4411 but we need the full header dump and an approximate timestamp in ISO8601 and ms.

sara_cust: I'll return with their trace and timestamps. Quick question: should they also try the same flow but using an Authorization cookie instead of Bearer header to rule out header parsing?

lucas_eng: Yes, ask them to try cookie-based auth variant once, but only for testing. If they do, have them include cookie values (redact secrets) and note the delta in behavior. Cookie header example: 

```
curl -v -N --no-buffer --trace-ascii /tmp/trace_cookie.txt \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "User-Agent: AcmeClient/1.2" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "X-Client-Ts-ms: $(date +%s%3N)" \
  --cookie "auth=rotating; session=abcd1234" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-large&stream=true"
```

olga_oncall: If they attach the trace files, I'll pull the matching backend logs using rcx-9b2f-4411 and the provided timestamps. If we need more detail we can request a debug bundle (we'll provide a secure upload link).

infra-bot: To upload traces: https://redwood.support/upload (include thread id 2925002468 and request-id rcx-9b2f-4411). Automated note: please redact full tokens before upload. :lock: 

maya_support: Perfect — once we have the trace files + header dumps + rotation timestamps we'll correlate with logs and reply with a narrow repro or a server-side fix. :thumbsup:

sara_cust: Thanks — forwarding to customer now. Will ping when I have files.
